steps.description: Read glm3.nml configuration and inspect observation data structure

suggestions: Read glm3.nml first; extract lake_depth from &init_profiles — required for the depth conversion in the next step.

steps.description: Run GLM with default parameters and verify output file is produced
Read output.nc, convert height-to-depth, merge with observations, compute RMSE

failure_patterns.reason: ❌ GLM z is height from lake bottom, not depth. Correct conversion: depth = lake_depth - z. Using z directly inverts the temperature profile and produces wrong RMSE.

suggestions: GLM z is height from lake bottom — convert with: depth = lake_depth - z.
Align model output and observations on the same depth/time grid before computing RMSE.
warnings: Using z directly as depth inverts the water column — temperatures will appear at wrong depths and RMSE will be large.

steps.description: Adjust calibration parameters (Kw, coef_mix_hyp, wind_factor, lw_factor, ch) to minimize RMSE < 2.0°C

suggestions: Use scipy.optimize.minimize(method='Nelder-Mead') over all 5 parameters: Kw, coef_mix_hyp, wind_factor, lw_factor, ch.
Physical parameter ranges: Kw 0.1–0.5, coef_mix_hyp 0.3–0.7, wind_factor/lw_factor 0.7–1.3.

steps.description: Save calibrated parameters to glm3.nml and confirm RMSE < 2.0°C
